title: Optimised the drawing loop, may work on more phones now
author: johnesco
selftext:
Link: [https://vibecodedgames.itch.io/pavement/](https://vibecodedgames.itch.io/pavement/)

Spent a while testing on any phone I could grab (2) and realized, I'm not sure what phones this does or doesn't work on. 

This has been the longest bout of "Vibe Debugging" I've done. As some of you may or may not know, I'm 'trying to find the limits of "how complex of a game can you make with no agents, one prompt at a time, and without looking at the code at all".

If anyone can give it a quick play and tell me what their phone is and if they have any sound stuttering or dropped frames.

For those of you who haven't played it before, I wanted something quick to pick up, playable when you have just a few minutes. Single thumb control with no rubberbanding and no "turbo boosts" (though I'm debating that).

Roads and weather are procedurally generated.

Settings will let you adjust from arcade vs "real" steering. You can also pick form many mobile control schemes and turn on/off many features to play the game to your liking.

* **"Quick Race"** lets' to get instantly into gameplay to see what how this game plays.
* **"Rivals Race"** extends this to 10 races and you can pick the difficulty, these rivals remember how you've treated them so if you trade paint in race 2, you may find them tailgating or blocking you in race 3.
* **"The Law"** switch sides and go after these obnoxious street racers!

Works on desktop with keyboard, gamepads, and several control schemes for mobile.

Artwork and sound are all still in development as is the whole game.

Created one prompt at time in a little-known technique known as "vibe coding" \\s

Still under development.

If you have a suggestion or bug, please be sure to tell me which rival (name and color) was involved, and if you played on desktop or mobile.

comments.body: What habe you done? Your about to get an influx of no job, pitching, pathetic anti ai losers coming in to waste their time and cry 'slop!' You've opened the floodgates to hell

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: I'm used to it. But many people on this forum gave me a lot of good feedback and now it's in the game. Just wanted to share and open to any questions on how anything was designed or what direction it's going. While vibe coding doesn't teach you much about coding (or even atrophies it) it has opened me into the real of scope control, requirements, testing (we'll I'm a tester by trade). I'm an artist but I'm not designing anything because I don't even want to think about the art until the movement and feel is right.
